content_units: Personal Budget Review Snapshot
Here’s a compact review of your January–June 2026 spending. Two charts will give you the clearest view: one for   overall category trends over time   and one for   how each month’s budget is split  .
Recommended Budget Charts
Chart   Best Use   What it would show   Why it’s useful
Line chart by category   Track month-to-month changes   Separate lines for rent, groceries, transport, eating out, and utilities from Jan to Jun   Best for spotting trends, spikes, and stable costs
Stacked bar chart by month   Compare monthly budget composition   One bar per month, split into the five categories   Best for seeing which categories take the biggest share each month
What Each Chart Reveals
1) Line Chart for Spending Trends
- X-axis: month
- Y-axis: amount spent
- One line per category
- This would make it obvious that   rent stays flat  , while   groceries   and   eating out   vary more.
2) Stacked Bar Chart for Monthly Mix
- X-axis: month
- Y-axis: total monthly spending
- Each bar split into rent, groceries, transport, eating out, and utilities
- This would show how much of each month’s total is fixed versus flexible spending, especially the effect of   eating out spikes  .
Plain-Language Insights
-   Rent is your anchor expense   at 1200 every month, so it is the largest and most predictable part of your budget.
-   Eating out is the most volatile category  , rising from 220 in January to 340 in May, then dropping to 280 in June.
-   Groceries show a mild upward trend  , moving from 340 in January to a high of 390 in May, which may suggest food costs are gradually increasing.
-   Transport is relatively steady  , staying in a narrow range from 88 to 110, so it does not appear to be a major source of budget swings.
-   May looks like your highest-spend month  , mainly because both groceries and eating out are elevated at the same time.
Budget Pattern Highlights
- Your   fixed cost   is mainly rent.
- Your main   controllable category   appears to be eating out.
- The biggest monthly changes are driven more by   lifestyle spending   than by essentials like rent or utilities.
- If your goal is to reduce spending,   eating out is the clearest place to start  , followed by monitoring grocery growth.
